text: The avarice of mankind is insatiable.
author: Aristotle

text: He is not poor who has little, but he who hankers after more.
author: Seneca

text: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
author: Seneca

text: Rather than love, than money, than fame, give me truth.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: The mass of men lead lives of quiet desperation. What is called resignation is confirmed desperation.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: That man is richest whose pleasures are cheapest.
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: Money never made a man happy yet, nor will it. There is nothing in its nature to produce happiness.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: He does not possess wealth; it possesses him.
author: Benjamin Franklin

text: Labor is prior to, and independent of, capital. Capital is only the fruit of labor, and could never have existed if labor had not first existed.
author: Abraham Lincoln
source: First Annual Message to Congress, December 3, 1861

text: With malice toward none, with charity for all.
author: Abraham Lincoln

text: Of all forms of tyranny the least attractive and the most vulgar is the tyranny of mere wealth, the tyranny of a plutocracy.
author: Theodore Roosevelt
source: The New Nationalism speech, Osawatomie, Kansas, August 31, 1910

text: No man can be a good citizen who is not a good neighbor.
author: Theodore Roosevelt

text: Behind the ostensible government sits enthroned an invisible government owing no allegiance and acknowledging no responsibility to the people.
author: Theodore Roosevelt

text: This country would not be a land of opportunity, America could not be America, if the people were shackled with inherited privilege.
author: Theodore Roosevelt

text: The test of our progress is not whether we add more to the abundance of those who have much; it is whether we provide enough for those who have too little.
author: Franklin D. Roosevelt

text: We have always known that heedless self-interest was bad morals; we know now that it is bad economics.
author: Franklin D. Roosevelt

text: The only thing we have to fear is fear itself — nameless, unreasoning, unjustified terror which paralyzes needed efforts to convert retreat into advance.
author: Franklin D. Roosevelt

text: The measure of a man's character is what he would do if he knew he never would be found out.
author: Thomas Babington Macaulay

text: No man who continues to add something to the material, intellectual and moral well-being of the place in which he lives is left long without proper reward.
author: Booker T. Washington

text: There is no class so pitiably wretched as that which possesses money and nothing else.
author: Andrew Carnegie

text: The man who dies thus rich dies disgraced.
author: Andrew Carnegie

text: Surplus wealth is a sacred trust which its possessor is bound to administer in his lifetime for the good of the community.
author: Andrew Carnegie

text: It is a shame for a man to desire honor simply as a result of his noble ancestors, and not deserve it.
author: Aristotle

text: The secret of happiness, you see, is not found in seeking more, but in developing the capacity to enjoy less.
author: Socrates

text: He who is not contented with what he has would not be contented with what he would like to have.
author: Socrates

text: Until the great mass of the people shall be filled with the sense of responsibility for each other's welfare, social justice can never be attained.
author: Helen Keller

text: The country is governed for the richest, for the corporations, the bankers, the land speculators, and for the exploiters of labor.
author: Helen Keller

text: There is a lie in the smile of the man who owns all and gives nothing; there is truth in the tears of the man who owns nothing and gives all.
author: Leo Tolstoy

text: Everyone thinks of changing the world, but no one thinks of changing himself.
author: Leo Tolstoy
source: attributed — appears in Three Methods of Reform (1900)

text: The two most powerful warriors are patience and time.
author: Leo Tolstoy

text: If you want to be happy, be.
author: Leo Tolstoy

text: Work is the only remedy; there is no other.
author: Mark Twain

text: October. This is one of the peculiarly dangerous months to speculate in stocks. The others are July, January, September, April, November, May, March, June, December, August, and February.
author: Mark Twain

text: The cry of the poor is not always just, but if you don't listen to it, you will never know what justice is.
author: Howard Zinn

text: We know that no one ever seizes power with the intention of relinquishing it.
author: George Orwell

text: Who controls the past controls the future. Who controls the present controls the past.
author: George Orwell

text: In a time of universal deceit, telling the truth is a revolutionary act.
author: George Orwell
source: attributed — not verified in Orwell's published works

text: Some are born great, some achieve greatness, and some have greatness thrust upon them.
author: William Shakespeare

text: The robbed that smiles, steals something from the thief.
author: William Shakespeare

text: Poor and content is rich, and rich enough.
author: William Shakespeare

text: Property is theft.
author: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon

text: The history of all hitherto existing society is the history of class struggles.
author: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels

text: From each according to his ability, to each according to his needs.
author: Karl Marx

text: Capital is dead labour, that, vampire-like, only lives by sucking living labour.
author: Karl Marx

text: While there is a lower class, I am in it; while there is a criminal element, I am of it; while there is a soul in prison, I am not free.
author: Eugene V. Debs
source: Statement at sentencing, Cleveland, Ohio, September 18, 1918

text: I am for socialism, disarmament, and the abolition of the state, in its present form.
author: Eugene V. Debs

text: It is difficult to get a man to understand something when his salary depends upon his not understanding it.
author: Upton Sinclair
source: I, Candidate for Governor: And How I Got Licked (1935)

text: They have stolen the future. We are fighting to take it back.
author: Upton Sinclair

text: The world is a fine place and worth fighting for.
author: Ernest Hemingway

text: The rich are only defeated when running for their lives.
author: C.L.R. James

text: Almost everything that distinguishes the modern world from earlier centuries is attributable to science.
author: Bertrand Russell

text: Poverty is the parent of revolution and crime.
author: Aristotle

text: In a country well governed, poverty is something to be ashamed of. In a country badly governed, wealth is something to be ashamed of.
author: Confucius

text: He who is not satisfied with a little, is satisfied with nothing.
author: Epicurus

text: Wealth consists not in having great possessions, but in having few wants.
author: Epictetus

text: Make the best use of what is in your power, and take the rest as it happens.
author: Epictetus

text: Do not spoil what you have by desiring what you have not; remember that what you now have was once among the things you only hoped for.
author: Epicurus
source: attributed — appears in various Epicurean collections

text: I have no money, no resources, no hopes. I am the happiest man alive.
author: Henry Miller

text: Give me your tired, your poor, your huddled masses yearning to breathe free.
author: Emma Lazarus
source: The New Colossus (1883), inscribed on the Statue of Liberty

text: The only foes that threaten America are the enemies at home, and those are ignorance, superstition, and incompetence.
author: Elbert Hubbard

text: Freedom is always and exclusively freedom for the one who thinks differently.
author: Rosa Luxemburg

text: Those who do not move do not notice their chains.
author: Rosa Luxemburg

text: The most violent element in society is ignorance.
author: Emma Goldman

text: Ask for work. If they don't give you work, ask for bread. If they do not give you work or bread, then take bread.
author: Emma Goldman

text: Pray for the dead and fight like hell for the living.
author: Mother Jones

text: The good we secure for ourselves is precarious and uncertain until it is secured for all of us and incorporated into our common life.
author: Jane Addams

text: The way to right wrongs is to turn the light of truth upon them.
author: Ida B. Wells
source: Southern Horrors: Lynch Law in All Its Phases (1892)

text: There is always more misery among the lower classes than there is humanity in the higher.
author: Victor Hugo

text: He who opens a school door, closes a prison.
author: Victor Hugo

text: First comes a full stomach, then comes ethics.
author: Bertolt Brecht

text: The worst sin towards our fellow creatures is not to hate them, but to be indifferent to them: that's the essence of inhumanity.
author: George Bernard Shaw

text: The reasonable man adapts himself to the world; the unreasonable one persists in trying to adapt the world to himself. Therefore all progress depends on the unreasonable man.
author: George Bernard Shaw
source: Man and Superman, Maxims for Revolutionists (1903)

text: I have never read Marx's Capital, but I have the marks of capital all over me.
author: Big Bill Haywood
source: Big Bill Haywood's Book: The Autobiography of William D. Haywood (1929)

text: In nature, nothing exists alone.
author: Rachel Carson

text: The more clearly we can focus our attention on the wonders and realities of the universe about us, the less taste we shall have for destruction.
author: Rachel Carson

text: We are called to assist the Earth to heal her wounds and in the process heal our own.
author: Wangari Maathai

text: Nature is not a resource for the economy. The economy is a resource for life.
author: Vandana Shiva

text: What is the use of a house if you haven't got a tolerable planet to put it on?
author: Henry David Thoreau

text: When one tugs at a single thing in nature, he finds it attached to the rest of the world.
author: John Muir
source: My First Summer in the Sierra (1911)

text: Your silence will not protect you.
author: Audre Lorde

text: It is not our differences that divide us. It is our inability to recognize, accept, and celebrate those differences.
author: Audre Lorde

text: I am not free while any woman is unfree, even when her shackles are very different from my own.
author: Audre Lorde
source: Keynote address, National Women's Studies Association, 1981

text: No pride for some of us without liberation for all of us.
author: Marsha P. Johnson

text: I'm sick and tired of being sick and tired.
author: Fannie Lou Hamer
source: Speech at the Democratic National Convention, Atlantic City, August 22, 1964

text: The moment we choose to love we begin to move against domination, against oppression.
author: bell hooks

text: The question is not whether we can afford to invest in every child; it is whether we can afford not to.
author: Marian Wright Edelman

text: No one has a right to sit down and feel hopeless. There is too much work to do.
author: Dorothy Day

text: Hope will never be silent.
author: Harvey Milk

text: Anyone who has ever struggled with poverty knows how extremely expensive it is to be poor.
author: James Baldwin

text: The most dangerous creation of any society is the man who has nothing to lose.
author: James Baldwin

text: To be afraid is to behave as if the truth were not true.
author: Bayard Rustin
